pressure.title: Hydrocarbons never see the atmosphere
pressure.description: A closed drain system collects pressurised or hazardous liquids drained from equipment (maintenance, start-up, level controller drains) in a closed drum that is vented to the flare, so vapours are not released to air and oxygen cannot get in. The drum sits low so drains flow by gravity; the header has no pockets. Closed and open drain systems must never be interconnected (vapour/fire spread).

components.key_components: Drain header, underground drum in pit, vent to flare, pump-out pump, level

video_tutorials.title: Closed Drain System — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Closed Drain System.

A closed drain system collects hydrocarbons and hazardous liquids drained from process equipment through a closed, sloped header into a drum located below grade and vented to the flare, so nothing is released to atmosphere.
A level-controlled pump returns the liquid to slop or process.
Typical applications include refineries, gas plants and offshore platforms; chemical plants handling toxic or flammable liquids.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Vertical Pump-Out Pump (column into the drum; returns liquid to slop / process).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Closed Drain System works.
Drains open from equipment into the header.
Liquid flows by gravity to the drum.
Vapour goes to the flare.
The pump empties the drum on level.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Closed Drain System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Closed Drain System.
Check level and pump auto-start.
Inspect pit for liquid / gas accumulation.
Internal inspection of drum.
Watch for drum overfill: high-level alarm. Common cause: pump failure, big drain.
Watch for header plugging: slow drainage. Common cause: wax / solids, freezing.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
